cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: C1 chassis. Defining anionic Sodium Laureth Sulfate @2 with prominent buffers Cocamidopropyl Betaine @4 and Coco-Glucoside @10; no reinforcing strong anionic. Laureth-4 @14 is a low-ethoxylate thickener (not cleansing, not a buffer).

conditioningLevel.rationale: High: C2 met with a payload lipid in place of the silicone. Prominent cationic Hydroxypropyl Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride @6; prominent waxy payload lipid Hydrogenated Castor Oil @9; pearlizing route Glycol Distearate @12; listed humectant Panthenol @7; plus refatters Glyceryl Oleate @11, PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate @15. Counter-signal: Hydrogenated Castor Oil in a pearlized shampoo is often a structurant at low level and there is no silicone, so bounded care (moderate) is realistic.

weightPotential.counterevidence: W-RICH holds formally (material waxy lipid @9 + prominent cationic guar @6); two families converge; waxy lipids are more persistent than liquid oils (6.4).
weightPotential.whyThisBand: A prominent guar plus a waxy hydrogenated lipid and refatters plausibly leave noticeable but bounded residue.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Not high: reset is not limited (C1 chassis with two buffers, resetCapacity moderate), so W-RICH does not reach the high anchor; the only lipid is a single hydrogenated castor oil typically used as a structurant, with no silicone, protein or second cationic; convergence is not strong enough for a coating conclusion. Not low: guar + material waxy lipid are two families (W2).
weightPotential.confidenceLimitingFactor: Role/dose of Hydrogenated Castor Oil unknown; W-RICH with moderate reset sits near the high boundary.
weightPotential.rationale: Moderate: guar + waxy lipid vs ordinary C1 reset; W-RICH recorded as counter-signal.
